claims.claim: Yb-bodies have been reported to possess biophysical properties typical of phase-separated condensates.
claims.source: Yb-bodies have been reported to possess biophysical properties typical of phase-separated condensates, which likely facilitate the biochemical processes happening in these foci (Hirakata et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: The formation of Yb-bodies depends on flam RNA.
claims.source: Given that flam is the major piRNA source locus in somatic follicle cells, we and others have found that the formation of Yb-bodies depends on flam RNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Dennis et al., 2016; Hirakata et al., 2019; Sokolova et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations and reference to a figure showing experimental data.

claims.claim: flamBG carries a P-element insertion in the putative promoter of flamenco.
claims.source: Two previously described flam mutant alleles (Brennecke et al., 2007; Malone et al., 2009; Mével-Ninio et al., 2007) disrupt piRNA cluster transcription via P-element insertions near the 5′ end: flamBG, carrying an insertion in the putative promoter
claims.evidence: This is a description of a genetic allele supported by citations.

claims.claim: flamKG carries a P-element insertion immediately downstream of the TSS of flamenco.
claims.source: and flamKG, carrying an insertion immediately downstream of the TSS (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is a description of a genetic allele supported by a figure reference.

claims.claim: Trans-heterozygous flamBG/KG mutants show strong de-repression of somatic, gypsy-family TEs.
claims.source: These mutants show strong de-repression of somatic, gypsy-family TEs (Brennecke et al., 2007; Malone et al., 2009; Mével-Ninio et al., 2007; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D)
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations and reference to figures showing experimental data.

claims.claim: flamBG/KG mutants show disassembly of Yb-bodies, despite some of the protein still being present.
claims.source: which is accompanied by a disassembly of Yb-bodies, despite some of the protein still being present (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by reference to figures showing experimental data.

claims.claim: The production of piRNAs derived from the 3′ UTR of coding genes is unchanged in flamBG/KG mutants.
claims.source: Notably, the production of other classes of piRNAs, such as those derived from the 3′ UTR of coding genes, is unchanged in these mutants (Hirakata et al., 2019; Sokolova et al., 2019)
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Knockdowns of nxf1/nxt1 in ovarian somatic cells (OSCs) compromise Yb-bodies formation.
claims.source: Knockdowns of nxf1/nxt1 in ovarian somatic cells (OSCs), a cell line derived from the somatic compartment of the ovary that expresses a functional piRNA pathway (Saito et al., 2009), also compromise Yb-bodies formation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, H)
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations and reference to a figure showing experimental data.

claims.claim: Soma-specific knockdowns of nxf1/nxt1 in ovaries compromise Yb-bodies formation.
claims.source: with similar results reported in soma-specific knockdowns in ovaries (Dennis et al., 2016; Sokolova et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: The production and localisation of flam transcripts to Yb-bodies and the assembly of those structures are interdependent.
claims.source: These results, together with previous findings (Dennis et al., 2016; Hirakata et al., 2019; Sokolova et al., 2019), suggest that the production and localisation of flam transcripts to Yb-bodies and the assembly of those structures are interdependent.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results and previous studies.

claims.claim: Depletion of some NPC subunits compromises the assembly of Yb-bodies.
claims.source: We find that depletion of some NPC subunits compromises the assembly of Yb-bodies
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and related figures.

claims.claim: Loss of Nup54 and Nup58 specifically impacts flam export, but not that of bulk mRNAs.
claims.source: and that loss of Nup54 and Nup58 specifically impacts flam export, but not that of bulk mRNAs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-FISH and oligo-dT staining data shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 physically associate with Nxf1/Nxt1 as well as Yb.
claims.source: We show that Nup54 and Nup58 physically associate with Nxf1/Nxt1 as well as Yb
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and proximity labeling data shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Knockdown of most Nups resulted in pronounced cell death and disassembled Yb-bodies, with little to no effect on TEs.
claims.source: Knockdown of most Nups resulted in pronounced cell death and disassembled Yb-bodies, with little to no effect on TEs (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Loss of subunits of the Nup62 sub-complex (Nup54-Nup58-Nup62) and their scaffold Nup93-1 caused strong TE de-repression.
claims.source: Instead, loss of subunits of the Nup62 sub-complex (Nup54-Nup58-Nup62) and their scaffold Nup93-1 (Chug et al., 2015; Stuwe et al., 2015; Ulrich et al., 2014) caused strong TE de-repression (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures and citations about the Nup62 complex structure.

claims.claim: Only the depletion of Nup54 and Nup58 resulted in TE up-regulation without severely affecting cell viability.
claims.source: Among these, only the depletion of Nup54 and Nup58 resulted in TE up-regulation without severely affecting cell viability (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: TE de-repression caused by knockdown of nup54 and nup58 was comparable to that observed upon depletion of Nxt1.
claims.source: Of note, TE de-repression caused by knockdown of nup54 and nup58 was comparable to that observed upon depletion of Nxt1 (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Cells depleted of Nup54 or Nup58 showed a strong increase in the expression of gypsy-family TEs.
claims.source: Cells depleted of Nup54 or Nup58 showed a strong increase in the expression of gypsy-family TEs, which are known to be expressed in the somatic compartment of the ovary and regulated by flam (Figure 1D–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D; Lécher et al., 1997; Pélisson et al., 1994; Prud'homme et al., 1995).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures and citations about gypsy-family TEs.

claims.claim: siNup54 and siNup58 had only a moderate impact on protein-coding genes, with 42 genes de-regulated in each.
claims.source: In contrast, we observed only a moderate impact on protein-coding genes, with 130 genes de-regulated in siYb (more than fourfold and adjusted p value < 0.05), 42 in siNup54, and 42 in siNup58 (Figure 1D–F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: A substantial fraction of genes up-regulated by more than fourfold in siYb, siNup54, and siNup58 is found nearby transposon insertions.
claims.source: A substantial fraction of those genes up-regulated by more than fourfold is found nearby transposon insertions that become de-silenced when the piRNA pathway is compromised (49/126 or 39% in siYb, 16/39 or 41% in siNup54, 13/40 or 33% in siNup58) (Figure 1D–F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Knockdown of nup62 and nup93-1 caused de-repression of some flam-regulated TEs and much more pronounced mis-expression of protein-coding genes.
claims.source: Although knockdown of nup62 and nup93-1 also caused de-repression of some flam-regulated TEs, we found much more pronounced mis-expression of protein-coding genes, with 207 genes de-regulated in siNup62 and 417 in siNup93-1 (more than fourfold and adjusted p value < 0.05) (Figure 1G, H)
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: siNup62 and siNup93-1 resulted in de-repression of TEs that are not normally subject to piRNA-mediated silencing in somatic cells, for example, R2-element.
claims.source: Furthermore, this was accompanied by de-repression of TEs that are not normally subject to piRNA-mediated silencing in somatic cells, for example, R2-element (Figure 1G, H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: siNup62 and siNup93-1 resulted in expression changes of other Nups, RNA export factors, and Yb.
claims.source: Of note, siNup62 and siNup93-1 resulted in expression changes of other Nups, RNA export factors, and Yb, presumably via indirect effects on nuclear transport and/or gene expression (Figure 1I).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 belong to the highly conserved class of 'FG-Nups'.
claims.source: Nup54 and Nup58 belong to the highly conserved class of 'FG-Nups' (Beck and Hurt, 2017; Figure 2A)
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation and reference to a figure.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 constitute the heterotrimeric Nup62 complex (Nup54-Nup58-Nup62).
claims.source: and constitute the heterotrimeric Nup62 complex (Nup54-Nup58-Nup62) (Chug et al., 2015; Stuwe et al., 2015; Ulrich et al., 2014) that lines the inner channel of the NPC (Beck and Hurt, 2017; Grandi et al., 1995; Kim et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claims.claim: The phenylalanine-glycine (FG) repeats of the Nup62 complex subunits contribute to the selective permeability barrier of the NPC.
claims.source: The phenylalanine-glycine (FG) repeats of the Nup62 complex subunits contribute to the selective permeability barrier of the NPC and interact with nuclear transport receptors, such as Nxf1 (Köhler and Hurt, 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: RNA-seq showed a reduction in steady-state levels of flam transcript upon nup54, nup58, nup62, nup93-1, and yb knockdowns in OSCs.
claims.source: Our RNA-seq showed a reduction in steady-state levels of flam transcript upon nup54, nup58, nup62, nup93-1, and yb knockdowns in OSCs (Figure 1D-H, Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: The reduction in flam transcript levels upon nup54, nup58, nup62, nup93-1, and yb knockdowns was specific to flam as other somatic piRNA source loci were unaffected.
claims.source: This was both specific to flam as other somatic piRNA source loci (e.g. the protein-coding gene tj or the piRNA cluster 20A) were unaffected (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, D)
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Depletion of Yb, Nup54, and Nup58 revealed a reduction in flam RNA that was more pronounced towards the 3′ end of flam.
claims.source: In contrast, depletion of Yb, Nup54, and Nup58 revealed a reduction that was more pronounced towards the 3′ end of flam (Figure 2B, C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: In nup62 and nup93-1 knockdowns, reduced flam RNA levels were uniform.
claims.source: In nup62 and nup93-1 knockdowns, reduced RNA levels were uniform, again highlighting a different role for these Nups (Figure 2B, C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Knockdown of nup54, nup58, or yb had little to no effect on PRO-seq signal around the transcription initiation site or within the first 10 kb and 40 kb of flam.
claims.source: Knockdown of nup54, nup58, or yb had little to no effect on either signal around the transcription initiation site or within the first 10 kb and 40 kb of flam, whereas a more pronounced decrease in siYb cells was observed upon inspection of the entire locus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G, H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PRO-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Global PRO-seq signal from protein-coding genes and cluster 20A was unchanged upon nup54, nup58, or yb knockdown.
claims.source: In contrast, global PRO-seq signal from protein-coding genes and cluster 20A was unchanged (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PRO-seq data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Loss of Nup54 or Nup58 reduces the stability of flam transcripts, with larger effects on regions distal from the transcription initiation sites.
claims.source: Overall, these observations are consistent with a hypothesis that loss of Nup54 or Nup58 reduces the stability of flam transcripts, with larger effects on regions distal from the transcription initiation sites.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the RNA-seq and PRO-seq data.

claims.claim: Depletion of Yb caused a collapse in the antisense, TE-targeting piRNA population, but leaving 21-nt siRNAs unaffected.
claims.source: As previously reported (Hirakata et al., 2019), depletion of Yb caused a collapse in the antisense, TE-targeting piRNA population, but leaving 21-nt siRNAs unaffected (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by small RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures and a citation.

claims.claim: Knockdown of nup54 and nup58 resulted in a approximately threefold decrease in antisense piRNAs, but this impact was highly specific to those derived from flam.
claims.source: Knockdown of nup54 and nup58 resulted in a approximately threefold decrease in antisense piRNAs, but this impact was highly specific to those derived from flam (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by small RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: piRNAs derived from tj and cluster 20A were unaffected or slightly more abundant upon nup54 and nup58 knockdown.
claims.source: In contrast, piRNAs derived from tj and cluster 20A were unaffected or slightly more abundant (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by small RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: piRNAs were lost homogenously along the entire flam cluster in siYb.
claims.source: Binning analysis of the flam locus showed that piRNAs were lost homogenously along the entire cluster in siYb (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 2E)
claims.evidence: This is supported by small RNA-seq data analysis shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: piRNA loss upon nup54 and nup58 knockdown was more pronounced towards the 3′ region of flam.
claims.source: In contrast, piRNA loss upon nup54 and nup58 knockdown was more pronounced towards the 3′ region (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 2E), mirroring the precursor transcript reduction observed by RNA-seq.
claims.evidence: This is supported by small RNA-seq data analysis shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Depletion of Nup54 and Nup58 resulted in clustering of flam RNA signal in one predominant focus within the nuclear envelope.
claims.source: Depletion of Nup54 and Nup58 resulted in clustering of the signal in one predominant focus within the nuclear envelope (Figure 2I–L, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: The flam RNA nuclear focus upon Nup54 and Nup58 depletion likely corresponds to flam RNPs stalled prior to nuclear export.
claims.source: Since the flam DNA locus is located at the nuclear periphery (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B, C), this RNA nuclear focus likely corresponds to flam RNPs stalled prior to nuclear export (Dennis et al., 2016; Dennis et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is an inference supported by DNA-FISH data and citations.

claims.claim: Neither nup54 nor nup58 knockdown affected the distribution of bulk polyadenylated mRNAs.
claims.source: Of note, neither nup54 nor nup58 knockdown affected the distribution of bulk polyadenylated mRNAs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Figure 2L, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A)
claims.evidence: This is supported by oligo-dT staining data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Depletion of Nxf1 or Nxt1 resulted in nuclear retention of newly synthesised mRNA.
claims.source: unlike depletion of Nxf1 or Nxt1, which instead resulted in nuclear retention of newly synthesised mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Figure 2M), as reported (Herold et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by oligo-dT staining data shown in the referenced figures and a citation.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 might be required to ensure processivity of nuclear export of the long flam transcript.
claims.source: Given that the effect is most prominent on the 3′ end of the transcript, we hypothesise that Nup54 and Nup58 might be required to ensure processivity of nuclear export of this, otherwise unstable, long transcript.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed data patterns.

claims.claim: Deleting the FG-repeats in Nup54 and Nup58 (∆FG) had little effect on their TE silencing capability compared to FL Nups.
claims.source: Likewise, deleting the FG-repeats in Nup54 and Nup58 (∆FG) had little effect on their TE silencing capability compared to FL Nups.
claims.evidence: This is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 lacking the C-terminal domain (∆C) failed to rescue transposon de-repression.
claims.source: In contrast, Nup54 and Nup58 lacking the C-terminal domain (∆C) failed to rescue transposon de-repression (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by rescue experiment data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: The ability to interact with the other Nups is required to ensure TE silencing by Nup54 and Nup58.
claims.source: These results suggest that the ability to interact with the other Nups is required to ensure TE silencing, and thus that Nup54 and Nup58 carry out this function from within the NPC.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the rescue experiment results.

claims.claim: The nup54MB allele produces a truncated protein lacking the carboxy-terminal region due to a Mi{ET1} transposon insertion.
claims.source: One such exception, the nup54MB003363 (nup54MB) allele, produces a truncated protein lacking the carboxy-terminal region due to a Mi{ET1} transposon insertion (Nallasivan et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is a description of a genetic allele supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The truncated Nup54 protein in nup54MB fails to co-precipitate with Nup58.
claims.source: This shortened Nup54 protein lacks the Nup54-family domain (Figure 3A, D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and fails to co-precipitate with Nup58 (Figure 3E), as expected from earlier reports (Chug et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3E and citations.

claims.claim: Trans-heterozygous nup54MB/9B4 flies were viable, although at reduced Mendelian ratios, and had smaller, but not rudimentary, ovaries.
claims.source: Trans-heterozygous flies (nup54MB/9B4) carrying the nup54MB allele over the nup549B4 deficiency spanning the entire nup54 locus (Nallasivan et al., 2020) were viable, although at reduced Mendelian ratios, and had smaller, but not rudimentary, ovaries (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by observations shown in the referenced figure and a citation.

claims.claim: RNA-seq from ovaries of trans-heterozygous nup54MB/9B4 flies showed TE de-repression and reduced flam RNA levels.
claims.source: RNA-seq from ovaries of trans-heterozygous nup54MB/9B4 flies showed TE de-repression and reduced flam RNA levels (Figure 3F, G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Expression levels of major dual-strand piRNA clusters (42AB, 38C, and 80F) were unchanged in nup54MB/9B4 flies.
claims.source: Expression levels of major dual-strand piRNA clusters (42AB, 38C, and 80F), which rely on different, specialised transcription and export pathways, were unchanged, if not slightly higher, in the case of 80F (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: Germline TEs were up-regulated in nup54 mutants.
claims.source: In this regard, also germline TEs were up-regulated in nup54 mutants (Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), confirming an earlier genetic link to TE silencing in germ cells (Czech et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figures and a citation.

claims.claim: The down-regulation of flam RNA in nup54MB/9B4 flies was more prominent towards promoter-distal regions of the cluster.
claims.source: Close inspection of the levels of flam RNAs using the previously described binning strategy showed that the down-regulation was more prominent towards promoter-distal regions of the cluster (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F), thus recapitulating our results from knockdowns in OSCs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Yb-bodies were reduced in nup54MB/9B4 trans-heterozygous flies.
claims.source: Lastly, Yb-bodies were reduced in nup54MB/9B4 trans-heterozygous flies (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: The yb transcript is mildly up-regulated in nup54MB/9B4.
claims.source: The yb transcript is mildly up-regulated in nup54MB/9B4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), thus loss of Yb-bodies likely arises as a result of compromised flam export.
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: The ability of Nup54 and Nup58 to form a complex is critical for their function in TE silencing.
claims.source: Overall, these data confirm a requirement of Nup54 and Nup58 for the expression and TE silencing activity of flam in both OSCs and in vivo. We find that the ability of Nup54 and Nup58 to form a complex is critical for their function
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the rescue experiments and mutant analysis.

claims.claim: The integrity of the FG-repeat regions of Nup54 and Nup58 individually is not critical for their function in TE silencing.
claims.source: but the integrity of the FG-repeat regions of each protein individually is not.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the rescue experiment data showing that ∆FG constructs can rescue TE de-repression.

claims.claim: The FG-repeats of yeast Nup49 and Nup57 (homologs of Nup54 and Nup58) are also dispensable for cell survival.
claims.source: Of note, the FG-repeats of their yeast homologs Nup49 and Nup57 are also dispensable for cell survival, leading to the suggestion that not all FG-Nups are equivalent and some can facilitate distinct translocation pathways (Iovine et al., 1995; Strawn et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies in yeast.

claims.claim: CLIP-seq experiments with HALO-tagged Nup54 and Nup58 failed to enrich for flam RNA.
claims.source: CLIP-seq experiments with HALO-tagged Nup54 and Nup58 failed to enrich for flam RNA
claims.evidence: This is a negative result from CLIP-seq experiments.

claims.claim: Independent CLIP-seq experiments with amino- and carboxy-terminally HALO-tagged Nxf1 showed an interaction towards the 5′ end of the flam transcript.
claims.source: whereas independent experiments with amino- and carboxy-terminally HALO-tagged Nxf1 showed an interaction towards the 5′ end of the flam transcript (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
claims.evidence: This is supported by CLIP-seq data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: Yb PL-MS enriched for the known Yb interactors Armi and Piwi but not for mitochondrial piRNA pathway proteins.
claims.source: Yb PL-MS enriched, among others, for the known Yb interactors Armi and Piwi (Hirakata et al., 2019; Saito et al., 2010) but not for mitochondrial piRNA pathway proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1—source data 1)
claims.evidence: This is supported by PL-MS data shown in the referenced figure and citations.

claims.claim: Only one Nup, Nup214, was detected as significantly enriched in Yb PL-MS.
claims.source: Only one Nup, Nup214, which localises to the cytoplasmic filaments and whose yeast homolog (Nup159) cooperates with the DEAD-box helicase Dbp5 in disassembling export complexes, was detected as significantly enriched.
claims.evidence: This is supported by PL-MS data.

claims.claim: Yb is not an integral NPC component but may nonetheless localise proximally to the cytosolic filaments of the pore.
claims.source: This result indicates that Yb is not an integral NPC component but may nonetheless localise proximally to the cytosolic filaments of the pore.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the PL-MS results.

claims.claim: PL-MS for Nup54 and Nup58 enriched for various subunits of the NPC, including all the components of the Nup62 sub-complex and the scaffold Nup93-1.
claims.source: Instead, PL-MS for Nup54 and Nup58 (Figure 4A, B, Figure 4—source data 1, Figure 4—source data 2) enriched for various subunits of the NPC, including all the components of the Nup62 sub-complex and the scaffold Nup93-1.
claims.evidence: This is supported by PL-MS data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: A modest enrichment of Nxf1 was detected in Nup54 and Nup58 PL-MS.
claims.source: We detected a modest enrichment of Nxf1, which is known to interact with FG-Nups and to export flam RNA (Dennis et al., 2016; Segref et al., 1997).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PL-MS data and citations.

claims.claim: Yb was among the most highly enriched proteins in PL-MS for both Nup54 and Nup58.
claims.source: Notably, Yb was among the most highly enriched proteins in PL-MS for both Nups (Figure 4A, B), thus indicating that Yb contacts the (cytoplasmic side of the) NPC in OSCs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by PL-MS data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Overlapping and/or adjacent signals between Yb and Nup54/Nup58 were often observed using immunofluorescence.
claims.source: Using immunofluorescence, we could often observe overlapping and/or adjacent signals between Yb and Nup54/Nup58 (Figure 4C)
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The Nup signal was found along the entire nuclear envelope and not exclusively in association with Yb-bodies.
claims.source: however, the Nup signal was found along the entire nuclear envelope and not exclusively in association with Yb-bodies (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Yb-bodies were often distinct from Nup foci.
claims.source: Conversely, Yb-bodies were often distinct from Nup foci, thus indicating that Yb is not stably anchored to the NPC but rather dynamic
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence observations.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 recovered a substantial amount of their respective partner Nup in co-immunoprecipitation experiments.
claims.source: As expected, Nup54 and Nup58 recovered a substantial amount of their respective partner Nup (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 detected interactions with Yb and, to a lesser extent, with Nxt1 and Nxf1 in co-immunoprecipitation experiments.
claims.source: We also detected interactions with Yb and, to a lesser extent, with Nxt1 and Nxf1 (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Co-immunoprecipitation of Nup54/Nup58 and Yb in OSCs was insensitive to RNase I treatment.
claims.source: Co-immunoprecipitation of Nup54/Nup58 and Yb in OSCs was insensitive to RNase I treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), thus indicating that their interaction is not mediated by flam RNA
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: 3xFLAG-Yb recovered HA-tagged Nup54 and Nup58 and only modest amounts of Nxt1, but not Nxf1 in reciprocal pull-down experiments.
claims.source: Reciprocal pull-down experiments in OSCs confirmed these findings, with 3xFLAG-Yb recovering HA-tagged Nup54 and Nup58 and only modest amounts of Nxt1, but not Nxf1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in the referenced figure.

claims.claim: The amino-terminal region of Yb contains a HelC domain, which is required exclusively for flam piRNA production.
claims.source: The amino-terminal region of Yb contains a HelC domain, which is required exclusively for flam piRNA production as opposed to piRNA biogenesis in general (Hirakata et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Deletion of the HelC domain in Yb weakened, though did not completely abolish, the interaction between Yb and the Nups.
claims.source: We observed that this deletion weakened, though did not completely abolish, the interaction between Yb and the Nups (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1F)

claims.claim: Yb interacts with the FG-Nups only when they are able to assemble into the NPC.
claims.source: Co-immunoprecipitation of HA-tagged FL Nup54/Nup58 or versions carrying the FG or carboxy-terminus domain deletions showed that Yb interacts with the FG-Nups only when they are able to assemble into the NPC as deletion of either Nup carboxy-terminus, which ablates interaction between the two Nups (Figure 3B), reduced the interaction (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: Yb associates with the cytoplasmic side of the NPC and binds to exiting flam transcripts.
claims.source: Although we cannot exclude the involvement of additional adaptor proteins that remained undetected by our approach, these data suggest that Yb associates with the cytoplasmic side of the NPC and binds to exiting flam transcripts.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the PL-MS and co-IP data.

claims.claim: Binding of Yb to RNA triggers the aggregation of flam-Yb RNPs into phase-separated Yb-bodies.
claims.source: Because binding to RNA triggers the aggregation of flam-Yb RNPs into phase-separated Yb-bodies (Hirakata et al., 2019), we hypothesise that this provides the directionality to flam transport.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on a citation and the observed data.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 are specifically required for TE regulation in the follicle cells of Drosophila ovaries by enabling export and subsequent piRNA production from flam transcripts.
claims.source: Here, we find that Nup54 and Nup58 are specifically required for TE regulation in the follicle cells of Drosophila ovaries by enabling export and subsequent piRNA production from flam transcripts.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claims.claim: The functional requirement of Nup54 and Nup58 for TE silencing is distinct from the general role of the NPC.
claims.source: This functional requirement is distinct from the general role of the NPC as other Nups, even those most proximal to Nup54 and Nup58 within the pore, are broadly required for gene expression and cell survival.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the effects of different Nup knockdowns.

claims.claim: A dedicated export-coupled licensing, involving Nup54 and Nup58, may allow the long flam transcript to be escorted directly from its genomic origin to the Yb-bodies to facilitate piRNA production.
claims.source: A dedicated export-coupled licensing, involving Nup54 and Nup58, may allow this long transcript to be escorted directly from its genomic origin to the Yb-bodies to facilitate piRNA production.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: If the Nup54/Nup58 export machinery is disrupted, flam transcripts are confined to the nucleus and destabilised.
claims.source: If this machinery is disrupted, for example, by loss of Nup54 and Nup58, flam transcripts are confined to the nucleus and destabilised, thus underscoring the need for a unified process from transcription to licensing.
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-FISH and RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: siYb caused a slight decrease of PRO-seq signal across the entire piRNA cluster locus.
claims.source: It is interesting to note that siYb caused a slight decrease of PRO-seq signal across the entire piRNA cluster locus, possibly indicating that disruption of flam export-coupled licensing negatively affects its transcription via a yet-unknown feedback mechanism.
claims.evidence: This is supported by PRO-seq data.

claims.claim: Nup54 and Nup58 interact with both the nuclear (Nxf1/Nxt1) and cytosolic (Yb) components of flam expression.
claims.source: We find that Nup54 and Nup58 interact with both the nuclear (Nxf1/Nxt1) and cytosolic (Yb) components of flam expression and thus suggest that these factors bridge nuclear export to cytosolic fate specification.
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-IP and PL-MS data.

claims.claim: The Nxf1-NPC-Yb axis coordinates initiation, processivity, and directionality of flam export.
claims.source: we propose a tentative model whereby this Nxf1-NPC-Yb axis coordinates initiation, processivity, and directionality of flam export (Figure 4G), directly feeding the transcript into the piRNA biogenesis route via Yb-bodies.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings, illustrated in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: The TE silencing function of Nup54 and Nup58 is carried out from within the pore.
claims.source: Our rescue experiments and protein-protein interaction studies argue for this TE silencing function of Nup54 and Nup58 to be carried out from within the pore, especially since neither Nup is among the most dynamic components of the NPC (Rabut et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from rescue experiments and protein interaction data, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Cytosolic Nup358 has been shown to be required for piRNA production from the dual-strand cluster 42AB in nurse cells.
claims.source: Of note, cytosolic Nup358 has been shown to be required for piRNA production from the dual-strand cluster 42AB in nurse cells (Parikh et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Depletion of Nup358 leads to prominent de-localisation of Piwi, which was not observed upon loss of Nup54/Nup58.
claims.source: Its depletion leads to prominent de-localisation of Piwi, which we did not observe upon loss of Nup54/Nup58, thus suggesting a different mode of action.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the effects of different Nup depletions.

claims.claim: Different NPC subunits can be co-opted for TE silencing in tissue-specific contexts.
claims.source: Nonetheless, this further underscores that different NPC subunits can be co-opted for TE silencing in tissue-specific contexts.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the findings about Nup54/Nup58 and Nup358.

claims.claim: Any transcript subject to strong selective pressure could evolve a dedicated export machinery via adapting FG-Nup functions in a cell-type-specific manner.
claims.source: We envision that in principle any transcript subject to strong selective pressure could evolve a dedicated export machinery via adapting FG-Nup functions in a cell-type-specific manner.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about a broader principle.

claims.claim: Several Nup genes in Drosophila show signs of rapid adaptive evolution that result in hybrid incompatibilities.
claims.source: Interestingly, several Nup genes in Drosophila show signs of rapid adaptive evolution that result in hybrid incompatibilities (Presgraves et al., 2003; Tang and Presgraves, 2009), which is often a hallmark of genes involved in genetic conflicts, such as transposon control.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: A tissue-specific control of export routes might contribute to explain the molecular mechanisms underlying nucleoporopathies.
claims.source: We further speculate that a tissue-specific control of export routes might contribute to explain the molecular mechanisms underlying so-called 'nucleoporopathies', human syndromes caused by mutated Nups (Beck and Hurt, 2017; Braun et al., 2018; Miyake et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations about nucleoporopathies.

claims.claim: In nucleoporopathies, mutation or expression changes of a Nup present in all cells leads to tissue-specific phenotypes.
claims.source: In these diseases, mutation or expression changes of a Nup present in all cells of the organism leads to tissue-specific phenotypes.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about nucleoporopathies supported by citations.

claims.claim: Tissue-specific phenotypes in nucleoporopathies might stem from specific roles of those Nups in regulating genes that are essential for the functionality of that particular tissue.
claims.source: We hypothesise that this might stem from specific roles of those Nups in regulating genes that are essential for the functionality of that particular tissue, which would in turn make the said tissue especially susceptible to the loss of the Nup.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

results.result: Nup54 and Nup58 are specifically required for transposon silencing in Drosophila ovarian follicle cells. Loss of these Nups results in compromised piRNA biogenesis exclusively from the flamenco locus, with minimal effects on cell viability or bulk mRNA export, distinguishing them from other NPC subunits that have broader effects on gene expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C36-C45, C105, and C106 collectively demonstrate that Nup54 and Nup58 have a specific role in transposon silencing via the flamenco locus. The evidence includes systematic knockdown experiments (C39-C42), RNA-seq showing specific TE de-repression (C43-C45), and demonstration that bulk mRNA export is unaffected (C37, C66). The specificity is further supported by comparison with other Nup knockdowns (C39, C40, C46-C48, C106).

results.result: Nup54 and Nup58 depletion specifically affects flamenco transcript stability and export. Loss of these Nups results in reduced flam RNA levels, particularly at the 3' end of the transcript, nuclear retention of flam RNA, but no effect on bulk mRNA distribution or transcription initiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C58 and C64-C68 provide converging evidence from RNA-seq, PRO-seq, and RNA-FISH experiments demonstrating that Nup54/Nup58 affect flam transcript stability and export. The 3'-biased reduction (C54, C63) is supported by binning analysis, PRO-seq shows minimal effects on transcription initiation (C56, C57), and RNA-FISH demonstrates nuclear retention (C64, C65). The specificity is confirmed by lack of effects on bulk mRNAs (C66, C67).

results.result: Nup54 and Nup58 knockdown results in a specific reduction of flamenco-derived piRNAs. The piRNA loss is approximately threefold and shows a 3'-biased pattern along the flam locus, while piRNAs from other sources (tj, cluster 20A) remain unaffected.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C63 are supported by small RNA-seq data showing specific effects on flam-derived piRNAs (C60, C61) with a 3'-biased loss pattern (C63) that mirrors the precursor transcript reduction. The specificity is demonstrated by comparison with Yb depletion (C59, C62) and other piRNA sources (C61).

results.result: The C-terminal domain of Nup54 and Nup58, which mediates interaction with other Nups, is essential for their TE silencing function, while the FG-repeat regions are dispensable. This indicates that Nup54 and Nup58 function from within the NPC.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C71, C82, and C83 are supported by rescue experiments showing that ΔFG constructs can rescue TE de-repression (C69, C83) while ΔC constructs cannot (C70). Co-immunoprecipitation data (C73, C96, C102) confirms that the C-terminal domain is required for Nup complex formation, supporting the inference that these Nups function from within the NPC (C71, C82, C112).

results.result: The nup54MB mutant allele, which produces a truncated protein lacking the C-terminal domain, phenocopies the knockdown results in vivo. Trans-heterozygous nup54MB/9B4 flies show TE de-repression, reduced flam RNA levels with 3'-bias, and reduced Yb-bodies.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C81 provide in vivo validation of the cell culture findings. The nup54MB allele produces a truncated protein (C72) that fails to interact with Nup58 (C73), and trans-heterozygous flies show TE de-repression (C75), reduced flam RNA with 3'-bias (C79), and reduced Yb-bodies (C80, C81). This confirms the requirement for Nup54 in vivo and validates the cell culture results.

results.result: Proximity labeling mass spectrometry reveals that Nup54 and Nup58 are in close proximity to Yb and Nxf1. Nup54/Nup58 PL-MS enriched for NPC components, Nxf1, and Yb, while Yb PL-MS enriched for Nup214 but not for Nup54/Nup58, suggesting transient interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C92 are supported by PL-MS data showing enrichment of Yb in Nup54/Nup58 PL-MS (C92) and Nxf1 (C91), while Nxf1 CLIP-seq shows interaction with flam RNA (C86). The asymmetry in detection (Yb enriches for Nup214 but not Nup54/Nup58, C88, C89) suggests transient interactions, which is consistent with immunofluorescence data (C93-C95).

results.result: Nup54 and Nup58 physically interact with both Yb and Nxf1/Nxt1. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments confirm direct protein-protein interactions that are RNA-independent, and immunofluorescence shows overlapping/adjacent signals between Yb and Nup54/Nup58.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C99, C101-C103, and C110 are supported by co-immunoprecipitation data showing interactions between Nup54/Nup58 and Yb (C96, C97, C99) that are RNase-insensitive (C98), as well as interactions with Nxf1/Nxt1 (C97). Immunofluorescence shows overlapping signals (C93) but also indicates dynamic localization (C94, C95). The HelC domain of Yb contributes to but is not solely responsible for the interaction (C101).

results.result: The formation of Yb-bodies depends on flam RNA and its export machinery. flam mutants and knockdowns of export factors (nxf1/nxt1) result in disassembly of Yb-bodies, indicating interdependence between flam transcript production, export, and Yb-body assembly.
results.evaluation: Claims C27, C30, C31, C33, C34, and C35 are supported by data from flam mutants (C30, C31) and export factor knockdowns (C33, C34) showing Yb-body disassembly. The interdependence is explicitly stated (C35) and supported by citations to previous work (C27, C33, C34) as well as data presented in the manuscript (C31).

results.result: Knockdown of nup62 and nup93-1 has broader effects than nup54/nup58 knockdown, causing widespread gene expression changes, de-repression of non-somatic TEs, and changes in expression of other Nups and export factors.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C48 and C55 are supported by RNA-seq data showing that nup62 and nup93-1 knockdowns affect many more genes (C46), de-repress non-somatic TEs (C47), and alter expression of other Nups and export factors (C48). The uniform reduction in flam RNA levels (C55) contrasts with the 3'-biased reduction in nup54/nup58 knockdowns, supporting the conclusion that these Nups have different roles.

results.result: Some Nups can acquire specialized roles in tissue-specific contexts, and the NPC has functions beyond constituting a barrier to nuclear/cytoplasmic exchange. Transcripts under strong selective pressure can co-opt NPC subunits to facilitate their expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C6, C115, and C116 represent broader interpretations of the findings. The evidence for tissue-specific Nup functions comes from the specific role of Nup54/Nup58 in flam export (C3, C4, C105, C106) and comparison with Nup358 in nurse cells (C113, C114). While C116 is speculative, it is a reasonable extrapolation from the demonstrated mechanism.

results.result: A proposed model suggests that Nup54 and Nup58 coordinate export-coupled licensing of flam transcripts through an Nxf1-NPC-Yb axis. This mechanism ensures processivity and directionality of flam export, with disruption leading to nuclear retention and destabilization of flam transcripts.
results.evaluation: Claims C107, C108, C111, and C104 represent a proposed mechanistic model. While the model is consistent with the data (nuclear retention upon Nup54/Nup58 loss, C108; interactions between components, C110; 3'-biased effects, C54, C63), key aspects remain speculative (C107, C111) or hypothetical (C104, C68). The model provides a framework for understanding the results but requires additional experimental validation of the proposed mechanism.

results.result: The authors speculate that tissue-specific control of export routes might explain nucleoporopathies, human syndromes caused by mutated Nups that lead to tissue-specific phenotypes despite ubiquitous NPC expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C120 are speculative extrapolations to human disease. While C117 is supported by citations about Nup evolution in Drosophila, and C119 accurately describes nucleoporopathies (supported by citations), the proposed connection (C118, C120) is hypothetical and not directly tested in this study. This represents an interesting hypothesis for future work but lacks direct experimental support.

results.result: Background information on NPC structure and function: The NPC is composed of ~30 different nucleoporins, serves as the gateway for nuclear-cytoplasmic transport, and has been implicated in gene regulation through chromatin association and other mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C7-C12 represent established background knowledge about NPC structure and function, supported by multiple citations to previous work. These claims provide context for the study but are not novel findings.

results.result: Background information on piRNA pathway and flamenco: piRNAs silence transposons in animal gonads, originate from piRNA clusters, and flamenco is the principal source of piRNAs in Drosophila follicle cells. Flam transcripts are exported via Nxf1/Nxt1 and localize to Yb-bodies for piRNA biogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C26, C28, C29, and C32 represent established background knowledge about the piRNA pathway and flamenco, supported by multiple citations to previous work. These claims provide essential context for understanding the study's findings but are not novel results.

results.result: Nup54 and Nup58 are FG-Nups that constitute the heterotrimeric Nup62 complex and line the inner channel of the NPC. Their FG-repeats contribute to the selective permeability barrier and interact with nuclear transport receptors.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C51 represent established structural and functional information about Nup54 and Nup58, supported by citations to previous structural studies. This background information is essential for interpreting the functional studies but is not a novel finding.

results.result: The FG-repeats of yeast Nup49 and Nup57 (homologs of Nup54 and Nup58) are also dispensable for cell survival, suggesting that not all FG-Nups are equivalent.
results.evaluation: Claim C84 is supported by citations to previous studies in yeast and provides comparative context for the finding that FG-repeats are dispensable in Drosophila Nup54/Nup58 (C83). This strengthens the interpretation but is not a novel finding from this study.

results.result: The amino-terminal HelC domain of Yb is required exclusively for flam piRNA production as opposed to piRNA biogenesis in general.
results.evaluation: Claim C100 is supported by a citation to a previous study (Hirakata et al., 2019) and provides context for the finding that deletion of this domain weakens interaction with Nups (C101). This is background information from prior work, not a novel finding.

results.result: siYb caused a slight decrease in PRO-seq signal across the entire flam locus, possibly indicating a feedback mechanism between flam export-coupled licensing and transcription.
results.evaluation: Claim C109 is supported by PRO-seq data but the interpretation of a feedback mechanism is speculative. The observation is interesting but the mechanism is not explored further, and alternative explanations (e.g., indirect effects on transcription) are not ruled out.

results.result: The TE silencing function of Nup54 and Nup58 is carried out from within the pore, based on rescue experiments and the fact that neither Nup is among the most dynamic components of the NPC.
results.evaluation: Claim C112 is supported by rescue experiments showing that the C-terminal domain (required for NPC assembly) is essential (C70, C71) and by a citation about Nup dynamics (Rabut et al., 2004). However, the authors acknowledge they cannot completely exclude a cytosolic function, introducing some uncertainty.

results.result: Cytosolic Nup358 is required for piRNA production from the dual-strand cluster 42AB in nurse cells, but its depletion leads to Piwi de-localization, suggesting a different mode of action than Nup54/Nup58.
results.evaluation: Claims C113 and C114 are supported by a citation to previous work (C113) and comparison with the current study's findings (C114). This provides context for the tissue-specific roles of different Nups but is primarily comparative analysis rather than a novel finding.
